title: Storage backend test matrix (Private DR toolkit) — backup/restore
content:
Last updated: 2025-12-14 (post DR drill + on-prem pilot feedback)
Owner: Sahana Iyer (CI/validation)  |  Backup/restore toolkit: rw-private-dr

Purpose
- Track supported backup storage backends + encryption modes across Kubernetes versions and deployment constraints.
- Record pass/fail and “gotchas” to feed docs + installer validation rules.

Assumptions / baseline config
- Private deployments on Kubernetes-in-VPC and on-prem.
- Backup artifact format per ADR-0137 (chunked tar+zstd bundles + manifest + checksums).
- Default job runner: Helm CronJob for scheduled backups + Job for restores (redwood-helm-charts PRs 433/447/452).
- Postgres backup modes:
  - Logical snapshot: pg_dump
  - PITR: WAL archiving to backend + restore sequencing (installer PR 861)
- Validation gates enabled for restore: health checks + smoke tests (installer PR 889) and maintenance mode toggles (PR 901).

Legend
- PASS: worked out-of-the-box with documented config
- PASS* : passed but needs specific config / constraints (see Notes)
- FAIL: currently blocked / not supported
- N/A: not applicable

Test cases (columns)
A. backup-create (rw-private-dr backup create)
B. backup-verify (checksums + decrypt/read manifest)
C. restore-in-place (maintenance mode + DB restore + artifacts + smoke tests)
D. restore-new-cluster (bootstrap + control-plane first + cutover)
E. retention-prune (safety rules; preserve last-known-good) (installer PR 872)
F. PITR (WAL archive + point-in-time restore)
G. scheduled CronJob (non-overlap / concurrency guard) (helm PR 447)
H. air-gapped workflow (offline bundle/export/import; no external endpoints) (installer PR 915)

Kubernetes versions covered
- 1.25 (oldest currently observed in customer fleets)
- 1.26
- 1.27
- 1.28
- 1.29 (current internal lab default)

============================================================
MATRIX 1 — Kubernetes-in-VPC (AWS-like)
============================================================

Backend: S3 (private bucket) + SSE-KMS (customer-managed key)
Auth: IAM role (IRSA) or node role

k8s | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | Notes
----|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|-----
1.25|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS|N/A| PASS* due to IRSA edge cases on older cluster templates. Ensure OIDC provider present + correct audience; otherwise fall back to node role.
1.26|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|N/A| Baseline happy path.
1.27|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|N/A| Baseline happy path.
1.28|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|N/A| Baseline happy path.
1.29|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|N/A| Baseline happy path.

Key gotchas / validation rules
- KMS key policy MUST allow encrypt/decrypt for backup role AND restore “break-glass” role (terraform example PR 327).
- Use VPC endpoint / gateway for S3 in restricted subnets. Without it: backup-create may hang then fail on timeouts.
- Cross-account KMS: PASS* only if key policy explicitly includes external principal + kms:ViaService conditions. Otherwise manifests as AccessDenied on UploadPart.
- PITR is sensitive to clock skew (restore target timestamp). Recommend NTP check in preflight.

Backend: S3 + SSE-S3 (bucket-managed keys)

k8s | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | Notes
----|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|-----
1.25|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS|N/A| Same 1.25 IRSA caveats; PITR requires bucket lifecycle tuned for WAL frequency.
1.26|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|N/A| PITR PASS* if bucket/object lifecycle does NOT expire WAL objects before RPO window.
1.27|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|N/A| Same.
1.28|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|N/A| Same.
1.29|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|N/A| Same.

Notes
- For regulated customers: prefer SSE-KMS. SSE-S3 is acceptable but evidence requirements differ.

Backend: MinIO (in-cluster) + SSE-S3 (MinIO-managed)
Auth: access key/secret (Kubernetes secret)

k8s | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | Notes
----|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|-----
1.25|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|N/A| Restore operations compete with MinIO IO under load; tune resources + PDBs. CronJob concurrency guard required.
1.26|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|N/A| Same.
1.27|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|N/A| New-cluster restore requires reachable MinIO endpoint from target cluster (not a single-cluster assumption). Usually solved via externalized MinIO or export.
1.28|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|N/A| Same.
1.29|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|N/A| Same.

Notes
- For VPC mode, MinIO is mostly for small/POC installs or when customer refuses cloud object storage.
- PITR PASS* because sustained WAL write rates can overwhelm under-provisioned MinIO (watch 99p backup duration + WAL backlog).

Backend: NFS (RWX share) mounted to backup runner

k8s | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | Notes
----|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|-----
1.25|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS*|N/A| PASS* due to file locking semantics differing by NFS server; ensure atomic rename supported for manifest swap. PITR not supported (WAL archival expects object-store semantics / immutability).
1.26|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS*|N/A| Same.
1.27|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS|N/A| Same.
1.28|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS|N/A| Same.
1.29|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS|N/A| Same.

Notes
- Restore-new-cluster PASS* only if the new cluster can mount the same NFS export (network/routing + credentials). Otherwise treat as “backup bundle export/import” workflow (on-prem section).

============================================================
MATRIX 2 — On-prem (connected but restricted)
============================================================

Backend: MinIO (customer-managed, external to cluster) + SSE-KMS (MinIO KMS integration)

k8s | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | Notes
----|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|-----
1.25|PASS*|PASS*|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS*| PASS* because KMS integration varies by customer (HashiCorp Vault transit vs HSM). We can’t assume “standard” headers/behavior; require preflight probe (rw-private-dr storage check).
1.26|PASS*|PASS*|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS*| Same.
1.27|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|PASS*| PITR PASS* depends on WAL throughput + MinIO erasure coding config.
1.28|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|PASS*| Same.
1.29|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|PASS*| Same.

Notes
- If MinIO endpoint uses private CA: ensure backup runner trusts CA bundle (mount) or TLS handshake fails (common in pilots).

Backend: NFS (enterprise filer) + at-rest encryption handled by storage layer

k8s | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | Notes
----|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|-----
1.25|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS*|PASS*| Air-gapped workflow supported via exporting tarballs from NFS to portable media (policy-driven). PITR not supported.
1.26|PASS*|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS*|PASS*| Same.
1.27|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS|PASS*| Same.
1.28|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS|PASS*| Same.
1.29|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS|PASS*| Same.

Notes
- Validation: require “no partial writes” guarantee. We rely on write-to-temp + fsync + atomic rename; some filers behave unexpectedly under quota pressure.

============================================================
MATRIX 3 — On-prem (fully air-gapped)
============================================================

Backend: Local file bundle (mounted repo) + offline export/import
- Backup target: /var/lib/redwood-backups (mounted PV or hostPath) OR customer-provided “staging repository” (NFS/SMB mount)
- Transport: offline media / internal transfer (customer procedure)

k8s | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | Notes
----|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|-----
1.25|PASS*|PASS*|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS*|PASS| PASS* because file ownership/SELinux differs by distro. Requires documented fs permissions + optional initContainer chown.
1.26|PASS*|PASS*|PASS*|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS*|PASS| Same.
1.27|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS|PASS| New-cluster restore PASS* if operator can mount the same repository into the new cluster; otherwise needs import step.
1.28|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS|PASS| Same.
1.29|PASS|PASS|PASS|PASS*|PASS|FAIL|PASS|PASS| Same.

Notes
- PITR: FAIL (not supported in fully air-gapped mode today) because WAL archiving expects continuous append to a durable backend with enough capacity; offline workflows break the RPO model.
- Documented workaround: increase snapshot frequency (pg_dump) + retain more snapshots; accept higher data loss window.

============================================================
Known issues / failures seen in testing
============================================================
1) Multipart upload + KMS AccessDenied
- Symptom: backup-create fails after ~5–20 minutes; “AccessDenied” on UploadPart/CompleteMultipartUpload
- Root cause: KMS key policy missing permissions for the assumed role; sometimes kms:Encrypt allowed but kms:Decrypt not, breaking verify/restore.
- Status: doc + terraform examples updated; add installer preflight check (planned).

2) CronJob overlap (backup duration exceeds schedule)
- Symptom: two backup pods run simultaneously; DB lock contention spikes; backups fail or restore takes longer
- Fix: helm concurrency safeguards (PR 447) + recommend backup window aligned with off-peak + increase schedule interval.

3) MinIO performance cliff for PITR (WAL)
- Symptom: WAL backlog grows; PITR restore incomplete / too slow to meet RTO
- Fix: scale MinIO (IOPS) + separate buckets/prefixes for WAL vs snapshots + compress WAL if acceptable.

4) NFS quota / inode exhaustion causing “partial backup”
- Symptom: manifest present but referenced chunks missing
- Fix: enforce atomic publish of manifest after all chunks present + verify step must be mandatory before marking backup as “good”. Retention pruning must never delete last-known-good.

============================================================
Recommendations (what we should claim as supported)
============================================================
- GA “recommended” (VPC): S3 + SSE-KMS + VPC endpoint + IRSA.
- GA “supported with constraints”: MinIO (external or in-cluster) with clear sizing guidance; NFS for snapshot-only (no PITR).
- Air-gapped: local bundle + staging repo workflow supported; PITR explicitly not supported (snapshot-only tiers).

Next updates / TODO
- Add automated CI job to run at least A/B/E on k8s 1.29 weekly (kind + minio + local filesystem) (Sahana/Rafael).
- Add preflight command: rw-private-dr storage check (S3 endpoint reachability, TLS, KMS perms, write/read test object) (Diego/Bruno).
- Confirm “strict tier” guidance for on-prem customers requesting PITR with MinIO+KMS (Fatima + Marcus).
